newsitem.title: JAPAN: Morgan Stanley advises long Japan stocks, short JGB.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley advises long Japan stocks, short JGB.

text.p: Morgan Stanley is advising investors to go long on Japanese stocks and short on the yen and Japanese government bonds (JGBs).

Barton Biggs, the investment bank's global strategist, said in a report issued on Friday that he expects the yen to remain weak "until the Japanese economy shows real signs of recovery and a resumption of inflation".
Biggs said in the report that as a strategy for investing in Japan he recommends "long stocks and short the yen and JGBs".

Biggs predicted that Japan's real gross domestic product growth would be "around two percent or maybe a shade better" and inflation as measured by the consumer price index would be around one percent this year.
The Japanese government has forecast GDP growth of 2.5 percent for fiscal 1996/97, which ends on March 31, and growth of 1.9 percent for fiscal 1997/98.
Biggs said the yen's weakness would eventually be bullish for the economy and stocks but bearish for bonds.
He also said share prices of good Japanese industrial companies, on a price-to-sales basis, are cheap compared with their international counterparts.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd JGB stood at 2.415 percent in early afternoon trade in Tokyo on Monday, down from 2.420 percent on Friday.
Meanwhile, the Nikkei average of 225 leading shares was down 88.94 points or 0.47 percent at 18,945.60.
